state.text:
## Shipped 2026-08-23

Five cards from the build queue, all of them view-level:

- **bb85** — `Shift`, `Alt` or `Ctrl+Enter` all insert a newline in chat; bare
  `Enter` still sends.
- **bb64** — this note. `state.markdown: true` renders it, with a Read/Edit
  toggle. Opt-in per tab, because plain is right for a paste and wrong for a
  report.
- **bb86** — right-click a card, a node or a tab: copy the id, copy a link to it,
  copy it as markdown, copy a subtree.
- **bb57** — those links: `#tab=bb71&node=bb57` selects the node and scrolls to
  it. Try [this link to bb58](#tab=bb71&node=bb58).
- **bb62** — export: copy or download a tab as `.md`, nodes as `.csv`, a diagram
  as `.svg`.

> Copy leads and download follows, deliberately: a VS Code webview may refuse a
> script-initiated download, and an affordance that silently does nothing is
> worse than one that was never offered.

The renderer is a subset — headings, lists, code, quotes, rules, links,
emphasis — built as DOM nodes rather than assembled as HTML, since every input
here is agent- or human-authored state. One fence type renders rather than
quotes: `mermaid`, through the same loader the diagram tab uses.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  tab[a board tab] --> ex[aboard export]
  ex --> doc[the project's own document]
```

---

Still open: 12 in backlog, `bb58` half done.

tabs.name: HTML example

state.html:
Sketch on it

A canvas, pointer capture, and a stroke that follows your hand — none of which a component catalog can express. That is the whole test for reaching for an html tab instead of ui.

Strokes persist through aboard.set() — reload the page and they are still here, because they live in this tab's state.data like any other board state. The frame has connect-src 'none' and no allow-same-origin, so it can do all of this and still reach nothing: no network, no access to the board except the bridge its parent handed it.

tabs.note: The case for an html tab: a canvas, pointer capture, and a stroke that follows your hand — things no component catalog can express. Draw on it; the strokes persist through aboard.set(), and the frame still has no network access at all.

A component the catalog does not have renders as a visible marker, never as nothing — an agent must not be able to believe it showed something it did not:
not in the catalog
That is the cost of the approach, stated honestly: the catalog is a closed vocabulary. When a shape is not in it, use an html tab.
